title: White chocolate and raspberry cake
subtitle: a white chocolate sponge layered with raspberry jam and white chocolate buttercream
excerpt: White chocolate and raspberry cake is two layers of white chocolate sponge sandwiched with raspberry jam and a white chocolate buttercream. White chocolate is melted into the batter to add a milky sweetness and a denser crumb than a plain Victoria sponge. The sharpness of the raspberries cuts through the richness of the white chocolate.
sourceNotes: White chocolate became widely commercially available in Britain from the 1980s onward. Its combination with raspberries became a popular pairing in British baking and restaurant desserts through the 1990s and 2000s, reflecting the wider influence of French patisserie on British home baking.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Sponges can be baked the day before and stored wrapped at room temperature. Assemble on the day.

content.text: White chocolate and raspberry cake is a two-layer sponge with melted white chocolate in the batter, filled with raspberry jam and a white chocolate buttercream. Melting the white chocolate into the batter gives the crumb a denser, slightly fudgier texture than a standard sponge. The sharp raspberry jam cuts through the sweetness of the white chocolate in both the cake and the buttercream.
Melt the 150 g of white chocolate for the sponge over a bain-marie or in short bursts in the microwave. Stir until smooth and leave to cool to room temperature.
Heat the oven to 180 degrees C (fan 160 degrees C / gas 4). Grease and line two 20 cm sandwich tins.

Beat the softened butter and caster sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in the eggs one at a time with the vanilla. Mix in the cooled melted white chocolate. Sift in the flour and baking powder. Add the milk and fold until just combined.
Divide between the two tins and bake for 25 to 30 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tins for 15 minutes, then turn out and cool completely on a rack.

Make the buttercream: melt and cool the remaining 100 g of white chocolate. Beat the softened butter until pale. Add the sifted icing sugar in two additions, then the cooled chocolate. Beat until smooth and fluffy.

Spread the raspberry jam on one sponge. Spread a generous layer of buttercream on top of the jam. Place the second sponge on top. Spread or swirl the remaining buttercream on the top. Arrange fresh raspberries if using.

attrs.problem: Batter splitting when the chocolate is added
attrs.avoid: Avoid adding hot melted chocolate to the batter; the heat can scramble the eggs.
attrs.fix: Let the melted chocolate cool fully to room temperature before adding. If the batter does split, add a tablespoon of the measured flour and beat briskly until it comes back together.

attrs.problem: White chocolate buttercream grainy or split
attrs.avoid: Avoid adding warm melted chocolate to cold butter; the temperature difference causes the fat to seize.
attrs.fix: Ensure the melted chocolate is at room temperature before beating it in. If the buttercream splits, warm the bowl briefly over hot water and beat again.
